_comment: CANONICAL REPAIR SPEC for the 86 hand-authored AP CSA past-paper FRQ pages
and their archive hub. Read docs/csa-frq-archive-repair.md first.
Every defect here was measured against live bodies on 2026-09-17 and is
recorded in docs/reports/2026-09-17-csa-frq-audit.md. Nothing in this file
is a guess about what a page contains: the generator reads the live body at
build time and REFUSES a page whose text it does not recognise, rather than
writing a repair over something it has not seen.
THE EXAM NUMBERS ARE NOT REPEATED HERE. They come from
copies of 7/7/5/6 is how one of them goes stale.
_titles: Target shape is the archive's own best form, the one 2023 to 2025 already
use: '<year> AP CSA FRQ <n>: <ClassName> Solution + Rubric'.
Two families are broken and they are broken differently. 2018 to 2022 ran a
slug-to-title pass that title-cased the whole handle, so AP became Ap and FRQ
became Frq. 2014 to 2017 kept the acronyms and still lost the class name's
internal capitals, so RandomStringChooser reads Randomstringchooser.
Class names are College Board's and are spelled the way the question spells
them. They are not retyped from memory: each one is asserted to appear in its
own page body before the title is written.

_stubs: Eleven pages whose entire solution block is a comment saying the case study
was withdrawn. There is nothing to solve and that is College Board's doing,
not a defect. The defect is the TITLE: four of them promise a Complete
Solution and the other seven promise a Solution, and neither is true.
They are not unpublished. That is on the NEVER_AUTO list, it throws away the
traffic, and a student who lands here is served by being told plainly that
the question is off the exam. So the title says so, and the page keeps its
explanation of which modern concepts the question touched.
The parenthetical uses a SHORT case-study label. The full name runs the
title past the 70 characters Shopify shows, and a title truncated mid-word
in the SERP is the defect this repair exists to fix.
ap-csa-2016-frq-1-randomstringchooser was checked and is NOT in this list.
It carries a real solution and already caveats, correctly, that only its
subclass part uses inheritance. It gets a title repair and nothing else.
_unitFix: Six pages state a Curriculum Alignment and link a Study This Topic guide for
a DIFFERENT unit, four lines apart on the same screen.
The page's own Skills Tested line decides, and in all six it says the same
thing. 2004 FRQ 4 and 2005 FRQ 4 are 'Array traversal', which is Unit 4, so
their ALIGNMENT is the wrong half. The four case-study pages are already
aligned to Unit 4 and link elsewhere, so their LINK is the wrong half.
Two of them link /pages/ap-csa-unit-1-study-guide labelled 'Unit 1: Primitive
Types'. That is the retired 10-unit curriculum, which this repo forbids in
front of students, and the handle answers 301 rather than 200. Both problems
go away with the unit correction.
_dates: Thirteen pages name May 15, 2026 as a future exam date, four months after it
passed. The next administration is Wednesday, May 12, 2027, Session 2, read
from College Board's AP Computer Science A exam page on 2026-09-17.
The archive hub also carries a static '46 days left' beside a script that
counts to the same dead date.
